content.value: Use Math.abs, sqrt, pow, and random; derive inclusive integer ranges without off-by-one errors.

The Math class provides static numeric operations. abs gives an absolute value, sqrt computes a square root, and pow raises a base to an exponent. Read parameter and return types: sqrt and pow return double. Arguments can themselves be expressions.

Math.random returns a pseudorandom double in [0.0, 1.0). To produce an integer from low through high, inclusive, multiply by high - low + 1, cast the product to int, and add low. The cast must happen after scaling. Each call samples independently; repeated values are possible.
distance is 4.5. The powers are 9.0 and 16.0, whose sum has square root 5.0. The die expression converts [0.0, 6.0) to integers 0–5, then shifts to 1–6.

Casting Math.random before multiplication makes the cast zero every time. Using high - low instead of high - low + 1 omits the intended upper endpoint. Random does not mean every outcome appears in a short run.
Write an expression for integers 10 through 15. Answer: (int) (Math.random() * 6) + 10. Identify the minimum and maximum before running any trials.
